entries.title: 中 휴머노이드 톱10 중 8곳, 韓 진출 채비…KC·상표·판매망 확보 - 전자신문
entries.paragraph_1: 중국 휴머노이드 판매 상위 10개 기업 중 8곳이 한국에서 인증·상표·판매처를 1개 이상 확보한 것으로 나타났다. 초기 단계인 국내 휴머노이드 시장에서 중국 업체들이 제품 인증과 브랜드 권리, 유통망을 선제적으로 확보하려는 움직임이 빨라졌다. 12일 산업 분석 보고서 '랩스딥리포트'에 따르면 중국 주요 휴머노이드 로봇 기업이 국내에서 KC 전파인증과 상표권, 판매 채널을 잇따라 확보하며 한국 시장 진입을 타진하고 있다. 세계 시장 출하 기준 상위권 기업은 이미 제품 인증까지 마쳤다. 애지봇은 지난 4월 중국 본사 명의로 휴머노이드 'X2 울트라'의 KC 인증받은 뒤 열흘 만에 한국 기업 아이엘과 독점 파트너 계약을 체결했다. 애지봇은 올해 상반기 세계 휴머노이드 출하 1위를 기록한 회사다. 유니트리는 지난해 12월 휴머노이드 'G1'을 본사 명의로 인증받았다. 부스터로보틱스도 소형 휴머노이드 'T1'과 'K1'의 KC 인증을 각각 2025년 1월과 올해 4월 완료했다. 국내 수입사 대신 중국 본사 명의로 직접 인증을 받는 건 한국 시장을 직접 수출 대상으로 관리하는 행보로 풀이된다.
entries.paragraph_2: 본체 인증 전 단계에서 상표와 판매망을 먼저 확보하는 시도도 늘고 있다. 갤봇은 코스닥 상장사 트윔을 한국 공식 대리점으로 두고 휠형 휴머노이드 'G1'과 산업용 'S1'을 국내 전시회에서 공개했다. 트윔은 G1에 자체 로봇 관제 플랫폼을 적용, 국내 고객사 대상 개념검증(PoC)을 하고 있다. 갤봇은 로봇 두뇌·운영체제 브랜드 '아스트라' 계열 상표 8건을 국내에 출원했고, 최근에는 한국 사업을 총괄하는 책임자도 선임했다. 유비테크는 국내 총판을 확보한 데 이어 휴머노이드 브랜드 'WALKER' 상표 등록 절차를 밟았다. 로케 역시 국내 기업 명의로 출원된 'ROKAE' 상표의 지정상품에 휴머노이드를 포함했다. 유비테크 '워커 S2', 갤봇 'G1' 등 공장·물류 현장을 겨냥한 대형 휴머노이드는 아직 KC 인증 전이지만 상표 출원과 총판 확보, 전시·PoC 등 사전 영업 활동은 이미 진행 중이다. 중국 기업의 국내 진출은 현재 대규모 판매 확대 단계라기보다 시장 진입에 필요한 인증과 브랜드 권리, 유통 기반을 선제적으로 확보하는 과정으로 볼 수 있다. 휴머노이드 완제품뿐 아니라 로봇 두뇌·운영체제 상표까지 먼저 출원하면서 향후 국내 시장 개화에 대비하려는 것으로 분석된다. 시장 진입 준비를 제품·소프트웨어·판매망 전반에서 동시다발적으로 추진하는 셈이다. 유효정 랩스딥 대표는 “중국 휴머노이드 기업들은 완제품보다 상표와 로봇 두뇌 브랜드를 먼저 한국에 들여놓고 있다”며 “국내 휴머노이드 시장이 본격적으로 열리기 전에 중국 기업들이 인증과 이름을 선점하고 있는 만큼, 한국 기업들은 경쟁사이자 잠재 파트너로서 이들의 움직임을 정확히 파악할 필요가 있다”고 말했다. 김명희 기자 noprint@etnews.com

entries.title: North Korea fires missiles days after South Koreaâs hypersonic test
entries.paragraph_1: SEOUL, Oct 12 (Reuters) - North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Monday, South Koreaâs military said, marking Pyongyangâs fourth launch in a month and following Seoulâs recent test of a hypersonic missile.
entries.paragraph_2: By Heejin Kim and Joyce Lee The ballistic missiles, whichappeared to be of different types, were fired at around 9:20 a.m. local time (0020 GMT) from near Pyongyang, and one type flew more than 900 km (559 miles), South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. Earlier, Japan's coast guard said North Korea had fired two unidentified projectiles, believed to be ballistic missiles, adding that both appeared to have already fallen. South Korea's National Security Office convened an emergency meeting, where it condemned the missile launches as violations of United Nations Security Council resolutions and urged an immediate stop. North Korea has been under UN sanctions since 2006, aimed at halting Pyongyang's development of nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles. The latest launches come at a time when tensions have been rising between the two Koreas in recent weeks amid weapons tests by both countries. Last week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country's first test-firing of a hypersonic missile , a rare public showcasing of a missile test by a South Korean president. Monday's missile launches by North Korea appeared to be "a show of force in response to the successful test launch of our hypersonic missile, as well as an intentional demonstration of missile capabilities," a spokesperson for South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. North Korea last fired a ballistic missile on October 3 , with state media KCNA saying it was a hypersonic missile tested under the supervision of leader Kim Jong Un . The tests followed a border mine blast last month that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul said the landmines had been planted by North Korea and demanded an apology, but Pyongyang has dismissed this and accused South Korea of provocation. Pyongyang has conducted missile tests on more than 10 occasions this year, including four in the last month. The unusually frequent tests indicate Pyongyang wanted to increase its leverage ahead of a potential summit between leader Kim and US President Donald Trump, said Song Seong-jong, a professor at Daejeon University in Seoul and a former South Korean Defence Ministry official. "They definitely need to raise the value of their status before meeting Trump," Song said. (Reporting by Heejin Kim and Joyce Lee in Seoul, Anton Bridge in TokyoEditing by Ed Davies)

entries.paragraph_1: South Korea gained independence in 1945 after being subjected to Japanese colonial rule for 35 years. Its first independent republican government was established in 1948. North Korean leader Kim Il-sung’s invasion of the South, which was spearheaded by Soviet-made tanks, took place in 1950. Millions of people died during the following three years. This was, in essence, an unforgivable atrocity in which brother fought against brother. The consequences of the war and the division of the Korean Peninsula were profound and enduring. Koreans who had collaborated with the Japanese Empire began to once again exert their power under the banner of eradicating communism. They went after pro-democracy activists, who were against dictatorship, branding them as “commies.” In the North, members of the Workers’ Party of South Korea were executed after being accused of being US spies. The North then became a hereditary dictatorship — the Kim dynasty began after being founded by Kim Il-sung, succeeded by his son, Kim Jong-il, and is now led by Kim Jong-un. Nonetheless, South Korean presidents understood that, one day, reunification should take place.
entries.paragraph_2: Efforts for reunification are exemplified by the July 4 South-North Joint Communiqué in 1972 and the first inter-Korean reunion of separated families in 1985. While Roh Tae-woo was president, South Korea established diplomatic relations with China and the Soviet Union, and both Koreas simultaneously joined the UN. Later, President Kim Young-sam agreed to participate in an inter-Korean bilateral summit, but that fell through after Kim Il-sung’s death. Presidents Kim Dae-jung and Roh Moo-hyun did participate in bilateral summits with the North, along with Moon Jae-in, who also arranged a summit between the North and the US. Summit-level diplomacy between Pyongyang and Washington broke down in 2019 in Hanoi, after which North Korea accelerated its efforts to develop nuclear weapons and missiles. During that time, the rift between the two Koreas only widened. As South Korean culture started trickling into the North, Kim Jong-un came to view it as a threat to the regime’s long-term survival and began implementing defensive measures. After revising the North’s constitution, Kim declared that the two Koreas share the relations of two hostile countries and began fortifying the border with the South along the Military Demarcation Line (MDL), the land border around which the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was formed. Based on its interpretation of where the MDL stands, North Korea has been planting mines north of the line and erecting barbed-wire fences along the border. We cannot begrudge North Korea for placing mines and barbed-wire fences on its own land. However, on Sept. 21, three South Korean military officials were injured after mines planted by North Korea in the western DMZ exploded. Why did this happen? The explanation is simple: the North and the South have differing views on where the MDL is located. Under the 1953 Armistice Agreement, the MDL was marked by hundreds of stakes set 200 to 300 meters apart from one another. entries.paragraph_1: This year has been the year of anxious middle powers. The more the two big powers, or three if you wish, talk to each other warmly but over other States, the more second-rung powers will consult each other. entries.title: Samsung Outsources Nvidia AI Memory Base Dies to TSMC as Foundry Yields Fall Short
entries.paragraph_1: Samsung's chief foundry rival now manufactures the most sophisticated component inside Samsung's own flagship AI memory product — a striking collapse of the vertical integration model that Samsung's memory division has relied on for decades. Seoul Economic Daily reported Sunday that Samsung Electronics agreed to source base dies for Nvidia's proprietary NVHBM memory architecture from TSMC's 3nm process, handing the contract to the Taiwanese foundry after an internal review concluded that Samsung's SF2 process cannot match TSMC's yield rates at the scale and reliability Nvidia demands.
entries.paragraph_2: The decision confirms what semiconductor researchers have tracked for months: a roughly 40-percentage-point yield gap between Samsung's SF2 gate-all-around process (estimated at 50 to 60 percent) and TSMC's N3 FinFET node (above 90 percent, per Nvidia's brief to suppliers) has become disqualifying for Samsung Foundry at the top of the AI memory market.

entries.paragraph_1: 서울 상암에서 오는 11월 말 국내 최초로 운전석에 사람이 없는 레벨4 자율주행택시가 시민을 태우고 달린다. 자율주행 스타트업 라이드플럭스가 운행을 맡고 제네시스 GV80 2대가 우선 투입된다. 19일 서울시와 자율주행 업계에 따르면 서울시는 상암 레벨4 자율주행택시 사업자로 라이드플럭스를 선정하고 오는 11월 말 서비스 개시를 준비하고 있다. 현재 사업자 선정 이후 세부 협상이 진행 중으로 계약 체결을 거쳐 본격적인 서비스 준비에 들어갈 예정이다. 앞서 서울시는 올해 하반기부터 상암 자율주행지구에서 국내 최초 레벨4 무인 로보택시를 운행한다는 계획을 올 초 발표한 바 있다. 상암 자율주행지구에서 3대 규모의 레벨4 로보택시를 시작해 2027년 10대 이상으로 확대한다는 복안이다. 올해 서비스에는 우선 제네시스 GV80 2대가 투입될 예정이다. 기존 양산 차량에 센서와 자율주행 시스템을 적용한 형태다. 차량에는 라이드플럭스가 개발한 자율주행 소프트웨어와 인지·판단 기술이 적용된다. 운전석에는 사람이 타지 않지만 운행 초기 조수석에는 안전관리자가 탑승해 돌발 상황 등에 대응할 것으로 전해졌다. 운전자가 핸들을 잡지 않는 레벨4 자율주행을 시민 서비스에 적용하면서도 초기 안전성과 시민 수용성을 확보하기 위한 것으로 풀이된다. 서울시는 내년부터 자율주행택시의 운행 범위를 한층 넓힐 계획이다. 차량도 1대 이상 추가하고 GV80 외 다른 차종을 도입하는 방안도 검토하고 있는 것으로 파악됐다. 실제 도로에서 운행 경험과 시민 반응을 축적한 뒤 웨이모 로보택시처럼 차량 안에 안전관리자가 없는 '완전 무인' 운행도 단계적으로 추진할 계획이다. 서울시는 상암·강남·청계천 등을 중심으로 자율주행버스와 택시를 운행해 왔지만 대부분 운전석에 안전요원이 탑승하거나 필요할 때 사람이 직접 차량을 제어하는 방식이었다. 이번에 시도되는 레벨4 자율주행은 운전자가 전혀 개입하지 않아도 사전에 학습된 구역 내에서 스스로 주행이 가능한 방식이다. 라이드플럭스는 현재 상암에서 관련 시험주행을 진행하고 있다. 운전석에 사람이 없는 상태로 다양한 혼잡 상황에서 운행하며 주행 경험을 축적하는 단계다. 라이드플럭스는 승객 운송뿐 아니라 고속도로 화물 자율주행과 물류배송 등으로 자율주행 적용 영역을 넓히고 있다. 서울시 관계자는 “사업자 선정은 이뤄졌지만 아직 계약 전 협상 과정이 남아있어 계약 체결이 이뤄지는대로 공식적으로 사업자를 발표할 예정”이라면서 “우선 조수석에 사람이 탑승하는 형태로 운영하고 내년에는 완전 무인으로 가는 방안도 생각하고 있다”고 말했다. 정현정 기자 iam@etnews.com, 김지웅 기자 jw0316@etnews.com

entries.title: Oakland Coal Terminal Backed by Trump Would Be Bigger, Dirtier Than Promised, Says Report | Post News Group
entries.paragraph_1: By Post Staff A recent feasibility study commissioned by potential investors says an Oakland coal terminal backed by President Donald Trump could export 13 million tons a year — three times the amount estimated in an earlier environmental review. Surprisingly, the report also contradicts developers’ and project advocates’ repeated pledges that the coal would be stored in a covered terminal. Instead, the millions of tons of coal shipped annually from inland states to the West Gateway terminal in Oakland would be stored in “two open-air bunkers,” with about 150,000 tons of coal per stockpile, before being sent overseas, according to the recent report cited by the L.A. Times. ( https://ruic.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Port-Study-RUIC-Bulk-Commodity-Ocean-Terminals-Study.pdf ) Residents and clean air advocates have long expressed concerns that coal dust would worsen pollution in West Oakland and throughout the East Bay. The proposed site of the Oakland Bulk and Oversized Terminal (OBOT) is located at the former Army base near the Port of Oakland, which developer Phil Tagami has been trying for years to turn into a shipping terminal despite determined community opposition. Trump announced a $75-million investment in the project in June , about a third of its estimated cost. The new terminal would be the largest coal export site on the West Coast, transporting coal to Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and Malaysia, according to the Trump administration. Trending Rockets Depth Proves Important in Playoffs Opponents say a new terminal would undermine years of progress cleaning up the air in West Oakland, which has a history of disproportionate pollution and high asthma rates due to its proximity to the port and other industry. According to No Coal in Oakland organizer Ted Franklin, who has been active for 11 years in the fight to stop the coal terminal, the report indicates that investors may be looking for a cheaper way to build the terminal. “We were shocked but not surprised” by the report, Franklin said. “Basically, it seems that the plan now is to store open piles of coal, which is a less expensive project than creating a completely enclosed facility.” The threats that the project poses are real, but it faces a lot of economic and legal hurdles, he said. Coal production is in permanent decline worldwide, he said, wondering who was going to “invest money in an industry that has no future.” Further, the project has not yet attracted big investors. “There’s no bank, no financing, no financial institution backing this,” he continued. A major legal hurdle facing the project is the passage of Assemblymember Mia Bonta’s bill, AB 40, the Community-First Coal Review Act, signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom on Sept. 30. The law requires developers of large-volume bulk coal facilities to complete a full Environmental Impact Report (EIR) under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) before they can operate. The law was specifically designed to block or delay the coal terminal project. The report to potential developers was produced by consulting groups Norda Stelo and Wood Mackenzie in July and released this month. It was commissioned by the Rural Utah Infrastructure Coalition, made up of eight Utah counties that are considering investing about $43 million into the terminal to receive Utah coal. The consultants produced their findings after visiting Oakland, examining engineering documents and holding discussions with Savage Cos., a Utah-based transport and logistics company selected to operate the facility Research has shown that coal terminal operations can be dangerous to public health. The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach moved away from open-air coal and petroleum coke storage three decades ago. The report says that the site could process 12 million metric tons, or 13.2 million tons, of coal each year, three times more than the terminal’s approved environmental impact report from 2002 and its 2012 addendum. Neither document mentions coal specifically, but rather bulk commodities. The coal arriving in Oakland could also be dirtier then had been previously stated, according to the report. Project officials previously said the terminal would handle only high-grade western bituminous coal from Utah, but the recent report says it will also handle Powder River Basin coal from Wyoming and Montana, known to be much dustier. Nor does the report mention plans to cover the rail cars to prevent pollution, though project officials previously promised they would only utilize coal transported in covered rail cars. “It appears the developers want to build something much bigger and more polluting than anything they previously revealed, either in court or to the West Oakland community,” said Colin O’Brien, deputy managing attorney at the nonprofit Earthjustice, speaking to the L.A. Times. The report indicates that the project may be much more expensive and take longer to complete than anticipated. The Energy Department estimates the terminal will cost about $231 million, but the report places the price at between $430 million and $625 million. The terminal will take 53 months to complete according to the report, significantly longer than Trump’s promise of exports beginning in 2028. Ted Franklin’s column, “Utah Study Blesses Investment in Oakland Coal Terminal but Leaves Key Questions Unanswered” is available at https://nocoalinoakland.info/utah-study-blesses-investment-in-oakland/ Post News Group Posts by Post News Group

entries.title: Kim Jong-Un 'rushed to hospital for emergency treatment', rumours claim - AOL
entries.paragraph_1: North Korean dictator Kim Jong-Un has sparked death rumours after failing to appear in public for a week. Unverified reports on social media suggest Kim was rushed to a Chinese hospital for urgent treatment after suffering a brain haemorrhage.
entries.paragraph_2: It was suggested that he was removed from the country because of the poor medical facilities in Pyongyang.
